subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the young anime witch girl whose appearance comes from <Picture 1>: long blue-purple hair in two thick braids, blue eyes, a black wide-brim witch hat with gold and white striped bands, a tan short cape over a white high-collared shirt with black ribbon ties and blue accents, a black scalloped-edge short skirt, and black short boots. She performs a silent dance with her lips gently closed and a relaxed, closed-mouth expression throughout.
<Subject 2> is the fantasy meadow environment from <Picture 2>, with turquoise-blue fluffy tree canopies on gnarled brown trunks, bright green grass, small purple, yellow and white flowers, rolling hills, distant mountains and a blue sky with cumulus clouds.
<Video 1> is the current RGB dance-reference fragment. Its dancer supplies the complete visible motion sequence, gesture timing, body direction, weight shifts and static frontal framing for this generated fragment.
<Video 2> is the synchronized depth rendering of the same current fragment as <Video 1>. It supplies body silhouette, limb placement, foreground depth and body orientation at the corresponding times. It is not a second performer or a separate choreography.
<Subject 3> is the dancer's choreography abstracted jointly from <Video 1> and <Video 2>, to be transferred to <Subject 1>.
<Audio 1> is the synchronized source soundtrack of <Video 1>, providing only the dance timing and background soundtrack. The final video uses the original source audio directly. Any voice or vocals in this track remain off-screen recorded audio and are not performed by <Subject 1>.

summary:
[reference generation + audio reuse] The target video places <Subject 1> in <Subject 2> and transfers the current fragment of <Subject 3> with the timing of <Video 1> and the corresponding geometry of <Video 2>. The generated fragment has the same duration as its supplied reference fragment. The final soundtrack is the matching portion of the original source audio, rather than a newly composed replacement. <Subject 1> remains silent with her lips gently closed for the entire fragment.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - retain the character identity, twin braids, striped witch hat, costume and boots. Her facial expression is relaxed with closed lips; speech and singing mouth movements are excluded.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - retain the meadow, turquoise trees, distant landscape and daylight.
<Video 1> (motion order and temporal structure): fully_preserved - preserve the current fragment's starting pose, gesture order, movement directions, holds, speed changes and ending pose.
<Video 2> (corresponding body geometry): fully_preserved - follow its silhouette and limb geometry at the corresponding moments of <Video 1>.
<Subject 3> (appears in [Shot 1]): attribute_transfer - transfer the choreography to the anime character while excluding the real dancer's identity, pajamas, rabbit mask, room and interface text.
<Audio 1>: partially_copy - the final output uses the source soundtrack trimmed to the exported video duration, without adding generated ambience, speech or music.

detailed_description:
The character has a clean 2D cel-shaded anime appearance within a detailed, cinematic fantasy landscape. Natural daylight, camera scale and exposure remain consistent throughout a single continuous vertical shot.
Throughout the entire shot, <Subject 1> keeps her lips gently together in a relaxed, closed-mouth expression, including during fast dance gestures and every segment transition. Her jaw stays relaxed and her mouth remains closed. Natural blinking, subtle eye expressions, eyebrow movement and head motion provide her facial expression. She does not speak, sing, mouth lyrics, count beats, open her mouth rhythmically, or lip-sync to <Audio 1>. Any vocals or spoken words in the source soundtrack are off-screen recorded audio; they do not originate from her. Transfer the reference body choreography while excluding any mouth opening or vocal performance from the reference.
[Shot 1] <Subject 1>, the blue-purple-haired witch with twin braids, striped black hat, tan cape and white costume, occupies the center of <Subject 2>. The static frontal camera keeps the same medium-full framing and body scale throughout. Her body orientation and limb positions at the first visible moment match the first visible pose of the currently supplied <Video 1>, using <Video 2> to resolve the arm silhouette, elbows, torso angle and weight-bearing leg. The motion is already underway wherever the supplied reference fragment begins; she does not introduce a new opening gesture or return to a neutral pose.

From that starting state, she follows <Subject 3> continuously in the exact gesture order shown in the current reference fragment. Her shoulders, elbows, wrists, hands, head, torso, hips, knees and feet move together with the corresponding reference body parts. Reproduce the height and direction of the hands, the extension of the elbows, the angle of each forearm and the turn of the torso at the matching points of the reference. Preserve left-right relationships as they appear in the source image rather than mirroring the choreography. Raised arms reach the source silhouette's height; lowered hands arrive at the matching body level. Weight shifts and changes of facing direction retain the source's timing instead of being replaced by generic swaying.

Maintain the reference cadence through every transition. A held source pose remains held for the corresponding interval, while a quick hand or shoulder accent remains quick. Do not add preparation time before a gesture, delay the next movement to complete a new flourish, repeat an earlier gesture, or compress the remaining choreography toward the end. The figure's secondary animation follows her actual movement: braids and cape respond with small natural motion while her hat stays secure and her costume remains recognizable. The background and camera remain steady, with no new cut, zoom or change of viewpoint.

The final body state matches the last pose visible in the supplied fragment. If this fragment begins partway through the full dance, continue that local portion rather than replaying the full video's opening. <Audio 1> supplies the original timing reference; the output soundtrack is assembled from the original source audio outside the generation step. No new character dialogue, commentary, count-in, sound effects or replacement music is introduced. The source's dancer identity, rabbit mask, pajamas, bedroom, captions, logos and interface graphics do not appear in the target image.

overall_soundscape:
Use only the sound already present in the reused source soundtrack. Add no generated wind, birds, fabric rustle, footsteps, speech or other ambience to the final audio. <Subject 1> is silent on screen, with no visible talking or singing mouth movements.

non_diegetic_music:
Reuse the original source soundtrack with its existing rhythm and timing. Do not compose, rearrange, restart or fade a replacement track. Treat all recorded vocals as background playback, with no lip synchronization by the visible character.
